title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms for paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We present the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, clarify why the bootstrap CI may exclude zero despite the nonsignificant McNemar (sparse discordant counts and bootstrap sensitivity), and explicitly label any one‑sided tests as exploratory because they were not prespecified.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation promises operational efficiency but carries safety risks: multi‑step sequence errors, protected‑field interference, and transient invariant violations can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and controlled studies document LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that affect code and configuration generation, motivating architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures [1],[2].

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) designed to isolate the incremental effect of deterministic downstream validation and a single allowed repair call under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Research question: when baseline and guarded conditions begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate, to what degree can a downstream deterministic validator plus at‑most‑one repair (guarded pipeline with a canary stage) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes compared with reusing the same initial candidate unmodified (baseline)?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus and archived validator traces. (2) Full artifact‑grounded execution accounting (completed pairs = 1000; hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005; repairs invoked = 5) and explicit reporting of generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate) and model configuration (declared model = gpt‑5‑mini; execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset — null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). (3) A clear inferential hierarchy: the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar is the primary confirmatory test; paired bootstrap intervals are preregistered descriptive summaries and any one‑sided tests are explicitly exploratory when computed post‑hoc.
sections.related_work:
Empirical and survey work documents hallucinations, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that degrade correctness for code and configuration tasks; these findings motivate verifier‑assisted generation and repair pipelines [1],[2]. Constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning have been shown to reduce syntactic/executable errors in other structured domains, though many demonstrations originate outside NetOps and thus depend on validator fidelity when transferred to network configuration tasks [3]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system proposals stress verifier‑assisted repair, guarded orchestration, and governance/proof‑carrying mechanisms as mitigations for automation risk; these works provide prototypes and architectural arguments that validator coverage and externally enforced protocols strongly influence operational reliability [4],[5],[6].

Our experiment complements this literature by preregistering a paired design that deliberately holds the initial sampled candidate constant across arms so that any paired difference is attributable only to downstream deterministic validation and the single permitted repair call.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The full preregistration (cand‑003‑stud‑001) was frozen before any hosted‑model invocation; its SHA‑256 is recorded in the execution manifest. Key prespecifications: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks drawn from a synthetic challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. Secondary preregistered summaries: paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) as descriptive.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and interpretive consequences. Under shared_initial_candidate exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both the baseline and guarded episodes; only downstream validator decisions and the single allowed repair call (guarded arm) could create paired outcome differences. Therefore, this study isolates verification/repair effects and does not measure gains that would arise from independent first‑pass generation changes (e.g., constrained decoding or different prompts), which were not executed.

Model and validator configuration. Declared model/provider: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). The archived model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Orchestration/adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5, a deterministic digital‑twin emulator that enforces required command presence/order, protected‑field noninterference, and workflow policies. Scoring rule: full_intent_constraint_validation producing a binary safe‑deploy verdict per episode.

Task corpus, selection, and execution bounds. Tasks were selected deterministically per the preregistered ordinal rule to produce exactly 1000 unique intents. The preregistration limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and specified missingness treatments (primary analysis: complete_pair_primary). Execution completed all planned episodes. Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1 implementing exact McNemar and paired bootstrap CI as prespecified.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact‑grounded). Run timestamps, manifests, raw outputs, provider traces, and validator traces are archived. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005; stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}. All deterministic consistency checks passed; contamination and missingness summaries are empty.

Primary paired outcomes. The 2×2 contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet two‑sided α = 0.05, so the preregistered H1 is not supported.

Preregistered secondary descriptive summaries and interpretive nuance. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01]. This bootstrap interval was a preregistered descriptive summary only. The apparent tension between a nonsignificant two‑sided McNemar and a nonzero bootstrap CI arises from discrete behavior with extremely sparse discordant counts: with n10=5 and n01=0 the exact two‑sided McNemar permutation yields p = 0.0625, while bootstrap resampling of paired outcomes can produce percentile intervals that exclude zero even when the exact test fails to reject because bootstrap percentiles reflect resampled distributions sensitive to rare discordant events. We emphasize the inferential primacy of the preregistered exact McNemar; the bootstrap result supplements but does not overturn that confirmatory outcome. Any one‑sided McNemar result computed post‑hoc is explicitly labeled exploratory.

Representative repair behavior. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred. Representative archived episode traces show the validator rejecting initial candidates for required_sequence violations or protected_interface touches and the adapter invoking the single permitted repair call; the repaired candidate then passed validation in those episodes. Total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). Details and raw traces are archived in the evidence bundle.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory vs descriptive evidence. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar is the primary confirmatory test and did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) was a preregistered descriptive summary whose exclusion of zero reflects bootstrap sensitivity with sparse discordant pairs; it does not supersede the primary confirmatory conclusion. A one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is reported only as exploratory.

Power and baseline prevalence. The preregistered power plan assumed baseline ≈ 0.60 and targeted an absolute effect of 0.15 for >80% power. Observed baseline = 0.995 substantially departs from this assumption, producing very few discordant pairs and greatly reducing sensitivity to detect small absolute gains in the paired McNemar framework. This mismatch explains the study's low power to confirm the small observed absolute improvement under the preregistered two‑sided test; we report this explicitly and with reference to archived power_and_precision_plan material.

Mechanistic implications within shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because both arms reused the same initial sampled candidate, paired differences can only stem from deterministic validator decisions and the single allowed repair. The five observed repairs indicate that a validator with appropriate coverage can correct some ordering/sequence violations. However, low repair counts constrain inference about repair efficacy across failure modes: it may reflect (a) few initial-candidate violations in the synthetic corpus, (b) generator behavior for the chosen model+prompt producing largely valid candidates, or (c) validator coverage limitations. Distinguishing among these requires follow‑ups that vary generation semantics, repair budgets, and validator rule sets.

Threats to validity. Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omitted policy checks would inflate measured success. Internal validity is strengthened by deterministic seeding and the shared_initial_candidate design but at the cost of not measuring first‑pass generation interventions. External validity is limited by a single model (gpt‑5‑mini) and a synthetic task corpus; generalization to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is untested. Conclusion validity is constrained by sparse discordant counts.
sections.conclusion:
In a preregistered paired study on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus using shared_initial_candidate semantics, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Five validator repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005. We emphasize the preregistered exact McNemar as the primary confirmatory result; bootstrap intervals and any post‑hoc directional tests are labeled and interpreted as supplementary or exploratory. Artifact archives (preregistration, raw responses, provider/validator traces, analysis artifacts) accompany this paper and support preregistered follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, repair budgets, validator coverage, and model families.

References

[1] R. Sapkota, K. I. Roumeliotis, and M. Karkee, "AI Agents vs. Agentic AI: A Conceptual taxonomy, applications and challenges," Informatics Fusion, 2025. 

[2] D. Anh‑Hoang, V. Tran, and L.‑M. Nguyen, "Survey and analysis of hallucinations in large language models: attribution to prompting strategies or model behavior," Frontiers in Responsible AI, 2025.

[3] S. Banjade, "Schema‑Constrained LLM Planning for Executable Molecular Workflows: An Intent‑to‑Execution Infrastructure for Cheminformatics," ChemRxiv, 2026.

[4] A. Harrison, "Protocol‑Mediated Execution Governance for LLM Agent Systems," SSRN, 2026.

[5] J. Augé et al., "Aether: Network Validation Using Agentic AI and Digital Twin," arXiv:2604.18233, 2026.

[6] R. Asadli, B. Hoffman, I. Protogeros, and L. Vanbever, "Evaluating Agentic Configuration Repair for Computer Networks," arXiv:2606.06212, 2026.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
